title: Audience Stitchbook: ML / Backend / Platform Messaging
content:
PURPOSE: quick, battle-tested messaging and brief competitive notes to help SDRs, AEs, and product demos speak differently to ML engineers, backend engineers, and platform teams.

OVERVIEW / FRAMING:
- Problem we solve (one line): predictable, low-cost, and observable LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Why it matters to each persona: ML engineers want fidelity and reproducibility; backend engineers want latency and reliability at scale; platform teams want standardization, policy controls, and cost predictability.

FRAMEWORK: SIGNAL vs LEVERAGE MAP (short):
- Signal = the primary metric each persona cares about (ML: eval/regression risk; Backend: p99 latency; Platform: cost per qps and SLOs).
- Leverage = the features we highlight to move that signal (ML: model versioning, evals, rollout canaries; Backend: smart batching, KV caching, kernel selection; Platform: private deployments, dedicated capacity, tracing + RBAC).

PRINCIPLES FOR MESSAGE TONE:
- ML engineers: precise, model-centric, empirical. Use bench numbers, eval hooks, and reproducibility language. Avoid vague cost talk unless tied to per-token unit economics and fidelity tradeoffs.
- Backend engineers: systems-first, operational. Lead with latency/throughput guarantees, deterministic behavior under load, and graceful degradation.
- Platform teams: governance-first, secure, and integratable. Emphasize policy controls, RBAC, network isolation, and billing transparency.

SHORT TALK TRACKS (30–60s) — can be memorized and adapted
- ML Engineer (quick): "We let you serve the exact model artifacts you validate with your evals and pin versions so canaries match your test-suite. Our rollout and regression alerts tie directly to your prompt sets so you catch quality drift before it hits prod."
- Backend Engineer (quick): "We run a GPU-optimized runtime with continuous batching and prefix caching to keep p99s low while the autoscaler ensures predictable throughput; if a model variant fails we failover to a compatible fallback—no app-level retries required."
- Platform Team (quick): "You get the same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, plus audit logs, KMS integration, and per-route cost dashboards so you can enforce policy and forecast spend centrally."

LONGER TALK TRACKS / DEMO FLOW (3–5 minutes)
- ML Engineer (demo agenda): show: model catalogue -> pin version -> run eval -> create rollout with canary and regression alert -> show eval diff and rollback. Callouts: reproducible seeds, deterministic tokenization, and eval integration hooks.
- Backend Engineer (demo agenda): show: latency dashboard under load -> enable batching config -> simulate spike -> show autoscale + graceful fallback -> inspect trace showing KV cache hit. Callouts: per-route SLOs, p99 targets, circuit-breaker behavior.
- Platform Team (demo agenda): show: tenant isolation -> private control plane UI -> RBAC policy set -> billing report for last 30 days -> show SLA and on-call integration. Callouts: VPC peering, HSM/KMS, retention policies for logs.

COMPETITIVE NOTES (concise, battle-tested)
- Generic large cloud AI providers: strength = integrated infra and scale; weakness = opaque perf for custom open models, fewer controls for private deployments.
- Simple LLM APIs (simplicity-first providers): strength = fast time-to-value; weakness = limited control over rollouts, lower transparency into p99s under tail latency.
- Self-hosted runtime vendors / OSS runtimes: strength = price and control; weakness = ops burden, patching, and lack of built-in rollout / eval infra.

POSITIONING NUGGETS (one-liners to use)
- "Ship LLM features with the predictability of a backend service."
- "Control the model you validated in CI, not the one that rolled out at launch."
- "Same API. Same behavior. Any deployment model."

OBJECTION HANDLING (short responses)
- "We already run models in-house": "Great — what are your current p99s and deployment pain points? Teams often underestimate the operational cost of rollouts and regression monitoring; we can save eng cycles or run a side-by-side to compare unit economics."
- "We need encryption/air-gap": "We offer private deployments with a customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integration, and air-gapped on-prem packaging."
- "Cheaper to self-host": "Maybe; but total cost includes engineering hours for ops, monitoring, and model regressions. We provide tooling that reduces ops overhead and a runtime optimized for lower per-token compute."

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS / TODOs (notes to self)
- gather 3 concrete p99 numbers from customers for demo slides (search latest SRE memos).
- collect one customer story where regression alert prevented a quality incident.
- update competitor matrix with new cloud offering that launched Q2 2025.

QUICK EXPERIMENTS FOR SDR / AE OUTREACH (low friction)
- Segment emails: send separate one-pagers: (A) ML eng: include eval-integrations doc + a short Jupyter notebook link. (B) Backend: include a p99 case study and a diagram of runtime flow. (C) Platform: include compliance checklist and billing UI screenshot.
- 2-week pilot offer: free dedicated capacity trial with guided onboarding and one joint runbook call.

ROLLOUT CHECKLIST FOR TRIALS (ops-focused)
- Pre-demo: pull model size and token distribution from prospect.
- Demo: show deterministic canary -> create regression alert -> simulate drift.
- Post-demo: provide short runbook, billing estimate, and contact in solutions engineering.

SNAPPY SLIDES / TALK-BULLETS (for quick deck)
- Slide 1: Problem: LLMs break assumptions of classic endpoints (non-determinism, stateful KV cache, tokenized costs).
- Slide 2: Our claim: "Inference you can reason about" (latency, cost, reliability).
- Slide 3: Persona-specific bullets (ML: evals + reproducibility; Backend: p99 & autoscale; Platform: private control plane + audit).

VOICE NOTES / SHORT PHRASES (pull-outs for outreach)
- "Model-proof rollouts"
- "Latency that behaves like a service"
- "Policy-first deployment"

APPENDIX: sample subject lines and openers (for outreach)
- ML: "Reduce model-regression risk with eval-driven canaries"
- Backend: "Cut p99 latency without changing your app code"
- Platform: "One control plane for hosted, dedicated, and private inference"

END NOTES: this is intentionally tactical and workshop-y. Add customer numbers and a short case study before marking final.

---
